data.name: Prasana
data.gender_notes: Prasana is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who offers or bestows a boon or a favor. The one who invokes, calls forth, or invites. A prayer, a request, a petition, a supplication, an entreaty. The name Prasana carries the meaning “Offering, Boon, Favor” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Prasana usually hope their child will grow to embody offering, boon, favor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the act of giving and receiving, and the importance of gratitude. Encourages the development of compassion and generosity.
data.etymology: Prasana belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Offering, Boon, Favor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Prasana total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Prasana is rooted in Sanskrit, which is one of the oldest and most revered classical languages in the world. In Hindu culture, the name Prasana is considered auspicious and represents offering a boon or a favor. It is believed that the giver of a Prasana, or a boon, is bestowing happiness and prosperity upon the receiver. This idea of giving and receiving is deeply ingrained in Hindu society and is often celebrated during festivals and celebrations.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Prasana lies in its connection to the concept of giving and receiving in Hindu spirituality. In Hinduism, it is believed that the universe is a manifestation of the divine and that all beings are interconnected. The act of giving and receiving is seen as a way to maintain this interconnectedness and to create harmony in the world. The name Prasana represents the invitation or petition that we make to the divine, asking for a boon or favor. It reminds us to keep an open heart and to offer our gifts and talents to the world, knowing that in return, we will receive abundance and blessings. The name Prasana also reminds us to be open to receiving the gifts and blessings of the universe, trusting that they will come to us in the right time and in the right way. Through the practice of offering and receiving, we can deepen our connection to the divine and to each other, and live a more fulfilling and meaningful life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Prasana: Receiving with open arms, symbolizing the pure and receptive nature of the soul, inviting blessings and knowledge.
